name: Vermont
nameStory: Vermont is French for green mountain - 'vert mont.' The nickname is not a nickname at all, it is just a translation of the name. Green Mountain State means Green Mountain State.
capitalStory: Montpelier is the smallest state capital in America, around 8,000 people, and the only one without a single McDonald's. The whole state's government runs out of a town the size of a large high school's worth of families.

majorFeatures.name: Green Mountains
majorFeatures.note: The forested spine running the state's length

majorFeatures.name: Lake Champlain
majorFeatures.note: Deep glacial lake on the New York border

funFacts: Vermont was an independent republic for 14 years before joining, with its own currency and postal service.
It was the first state admitted after the original thirteen.
It is the only New England state with no ocean coastline.
Congress declared Lake Champlain a sixth Great Lake in 1998. The outcry was immediate and the designation was repealed 18 days later.
whyItMatters: Vermont's 1777 constitution, written while it was still an independent republic, was the first in America to ban adult slavery outright - 88 years before the Thirteenth Amendment.
